subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should ordinary plugin runtime code be allowed to call plugin-registered Gateway methods, and if so should the SDK expose a raw dispatcher, a curated allowlisted gateway surface, or typed capability/service contracts?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the API shape changes the public Plugin SDK and Gateway authorization boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent contract or security policy.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
options.body: Expose approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller identity, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep HTTP-route dispatch only
options.body: Decline ordinary plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls and require plugins to use existing HTTP route, runtime helper, or capability seams.

options.title: Expose raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Add a generic method-string caller and accept the larger security and compatibility surface as a maintainer-owned product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized SDK contract
recommendation.body: Expose approved methods or typed capabilities with plugin caller identity, explicit authorization, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history for the current Gateway dispatch contract and Plugin SDK boundary points to steipete for the API/security direction call.
